name: Camicia
description: Camicia (Italian for 'Shirt') is a simple game of pure luck for two players. It is the Italian version of Beggar My Neighbour. Players turn over cards alternately; Aces, 2s and 3s are 'attack' cards that force the opponent to play 1, 2, or 3 cards respectively. If the defender cannot play an attack card in response, the attacker wins the pile.

content.text: Camicia (Italian for 'Shirt') is a simple game of pure luck for two players. It is the Italian version of Beggar My Neighbour. Players turn over cards alternately; Aces, 2s and 3s are 'attack' cards that force the opponent to play 1, 2, or 3 cards respectively. If the defender cannot play an attack card in response, the attacker wins the pile.

Camicia is the Italian version of Beggar My Neighbour (also known as Strip Jack Naked or Beat Your Neighbor Out of Doors), a traditional children's card game played worldwide. The name 'Camicia' means 'shirt' in Italian, possibly referring to the idea of stripping your opponent of cards.

Camicia is played by exactly two players. Each player receives an equal share of the deck face down (20 cards each with a 40-card Italian deck, or 26 each with 52 cards). Players keep their cards in a packet and do not look at them; they take turns turning the top card face up onto the table.
40-card Italian deck (suits: swords, batons, cups, coins) or 52-card standard deck. Suits are ignored. Attack cards: Aces, 2s, 3s. Normal cards: 4-10, J, Q, K (or 4-7, J, Q, K in 40-card deck).
All cards dealt face down to the two players, 20 cards each (if 40-card deck) or 26 cards each (if 52-card deck). Players do not look at their cards.
